oracle.description: test_defect_seeds.py decides correctness: 28 tests, red at the starting commit because defect_seeds.py does not exist. A permissive stub that parses nothing and always reports falsified fails 17. The stub that matters treats a command with no result as satisfied and fails 3.

purpose:
Write templates/dispatch/scripts/defect_seeds.py so a packet can prove its oracle actually detects the defects it claims to detect.

agentops#2046 asks for defect-seeded acceptance cases that fail deterministically. The existing acceptance-properties-discriminating pre-gate is structural only: it requires each acceptance property to name the behaviour it falsifies, and never checks that the oracle goes red when that behaviour is present. So a packet may declare a falsifying condition its own oracle cannot detect, and nothing notices.

A seed is the reference overlay's complement. The reference patch must turn the oracle GREEN; a seed patch must turn it RED. A seeded defect that leaves the oracle green proves the oracle does not test what the packet claims.

Ordering, patching and running belong to the coordinator. This module decides only what a seed declaration MEANS and whether evidence satisfies it. No git, no subprocess, no file I/O.

The seam is SEED_ID_RE plus three functions:
  parse_seeds(packet) -> normalised oracle.defect_seeds, each {'id','patch','expect_red','description'} with description defaulting to ''. A packet declaring none returns [] and is NOT an error. Raises ValueError when a declaration is present but unusable: not a list, a non-object entry, a missing or malformed id, a duplicate id, a missing patch, an absolute patch path or one escaping the repository, an empty expect_red, or an expect_red naming a command that is not in oracle.starts_red.
  seed_falsified(seed, results) -> bool. results is any iterable of {'command_id','exit_code'}, drained once. True iff every command in expect_red has a result AND every one is nonzero.
  unfalsified(packet, outcomes) -> the seed ids that did not falsify, in packet order. outcomes maps a seed id to that seed's results; a seed missing from outcomes is reported.

SEED_ID_RE takes the same shape as an acceptance property id: starts with a letter, then letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-'.

The likeliest wrong implementation treats a command with NO result as satisfied -- reading silence as evidence. A command that never ran has shown nothing and must not count as red.
required_outcomes: a packet declaring no defect_seeds returns [] and raises nothing
parse_seeds normalises each seed to exactly id, patch, expect_red and description
parse_seeds refuses a duplicate id, an empty expect_red, and an expect_red outside oracle.starts_red
parse_seeds refuses an absolute patch path and one escaping the repository
seed_falsified requires every expected command to have run AND to be red
a command with no result is never counted as red
unfalsified reports, in packet order, every seed that did not falsify, including seeds with no outcome

acceptance_properties.requirement: a seeded defect the oracle does not notice is reported
acceptance_properties.fails_when: a seed whose expected command stayed green is treated as falsified
a seed with no result for an expected command counts as falsified

acceptance_properties.requirement: a seed declaration is unambiguous or refused
acceptance_properties.fails_when: a duplicate id, an empty expect_red, an expect_red outside starts_red, or a patch path escaping the repository is accepted

acceptance_properties.requirement: packets frozen before this row keep their meaning
acceptance_properties.fails_when: a packet that declares no defect_seeds raises instead of returning an empty list

non_goals: applying seed patches or running commands -- that is the coordinator hand-pass
wiring seeds into hybrid_dispatch.py, which is protected at the manifest level
authoring the seed patches for any particular packet
